headlines.title: How Many Shares of Duke Energy, Consolidated Edison or AEP Pay $1,000 a Month in Dividends?
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysAt today’s prices, $1,000 a month in dividends takes 2,765 shares of Duke Energy, 3,093 shares of American Electric Power or 3,381 shares of Consolidated Edison. Duke Energy costs the least, about $358,800, which is about $44,700 less than Consolidated Edison, but it pays out the most of its earnings: 67% of fiscal 2025 normalized EPS.

headlines.title: A $1 Million Retirement Portfolio Could Generate $25,000 a Year Without Selling Shares
headlines.summary: The day the last paycheck lands, a saver's question flips from how big the pile is to how much cash it sends home. Five blue-chip payers, from a data center boom to a 70-year streak, each carry a risk worth knowing first.

headlines.title: How Much You Really Need Invested to Generate $50,000 a Year in Retirement
headlines.summary: Safe blue chips have rallied so hard that their yields now trail Treasuries, while the highest payers promise to slash the capital you need. Before you chase either, see what each shortcut quietly puts at risk in year ten.

headlines.title: $100,000 in These 5 Dividend Stocks Could Pay $4,800 a Year
headlines.summary: When the paycheck stops, price charts matter less than the cash landing in your account each quarter. Five high-yield names across pharma, utilities, tobacco, telecom, and midstream energy compete for that job, and one carries the thinnest safety cushion of all.

headlines.title: Traveling this Thanksgiving? Duke Energy Florida shares 4 tips to save energy while away
headlines.summary: With 81.5 million Americans projected to travel at least 50 miles from home for Thanksgiving celebrations this year, Duke Energy Florida is sharing four tips to help customers save energy while they're away.

description: Duke Energy Corporation, through its subsidiaries, operates as an energy company in the United States. The company operates through two segments: Electric Utilities and Infrastructure (EU&I); and Gas Utilities and Infrastructure (GU&I). The EU&I segment generates, transmits, distributes, and sells electricity to customers in the Southeast and Midwest regions. It generates electricity through coal, hydroelectric, natural gas, oil, renewables, and nuclear fuel. This segment also engages in the wholesale of electricity to municipalities, electric cooperative utilities, and other load-serving entities. The GU&I segment distributes natural gas to customers in the residential, commercial, industrial, and power generation natural gas sectors; and invests in pipeline transmission projects, renewable natural gas projects, and natural gas storage facilities. The company was formerly known as Duke Energy Holding Corp. and changed its name to Duke Energy Corporation in April 2006. Duke Energy Corporation was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina.
